Operator: Good day, and welcome to the AmpliFi Communications Q4 2023 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded. I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson: Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and welcome to AmpliFi Communications' Q4 and full-year 2023 Earnings Conference Call. Joining me on the call today are Johnathan Reed, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Torres, Chief Financial Officer; and other members of our leadership team. Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's discussion may contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more complete discussion of these risks.

Johnathan Reed: Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. I'm pleased to report our results for Q4 and the full year 2023. We achieved strong revenue growth and robust profitability, which reflects our strong execution in a dynamic market. We are particularly excited about the initial performance of our 5G Ultra Wideband service and its positive impact on subscriber growth and ARPU uplift. Our investments in network modernization and converged media offerings are also paying off, driving increased customer satisfaction and loyalty across our wireless, broadband, and streaming segments. Furthermore, we have focused on operational efficiency and capex discipline, which has allowed us to maintain profitability while expanding margins. Finally, our strategic focus remains on premium bundling, 5G standalone deployments, and international expansion to solidify our position as a leader in the telecom-media convergence.

Michael Torres: Thank you, Johnathan. Turning to the financials, our revenue for the quarter was $28.7 billion, representing a 5.2% increase year-over-year, with full-year revenue reaching $112.5 billion. Our adjusted EBITDA was $11.5 billion for the quarter, with a margin of 40.1%, up 250 basis points year-over-year, and full-year EBITDA of $44.2 billion. We continue to manage our expenses effectively and are on track to meet our financial targets for the year. Our capital expenditures were $14.5 billion for the full year, primarily driven by investments in our 5G network expansion, fiber-to-the-home rollouts, and edge computing infrastructure.

Good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining our Q4 and full-year 2023 earnings call for AmpliFi Communications. As your CFO, I'm pleased to dive deeper into our financial results, starting with a detailed breakdown of our revenue mix by segment, which highlights the percentage contributions, year-over-year trends, and strategic drivers behind them. This analysis underscores our balanced portfolio across telecommunications and media, delivering resilient growth amid 5G acceleration, fiber-to-the-x expansions, and the shift to streaming despite cord-cutting pressures.

For Q4, total revenues reached $28.7 billion, up 5.2% year-over-year, driven by a favorable mix shift toward high-margin segments. Wireless services contributed 42% of total revenues at $12.1 billion, up 5.8% year-over-year. This remains our largest contributor, reflecting strong postpaid subscriber net adds of 1.2 million—our best Q4 in five years—fueled by our mid-band 5G Ultra Wideband network, now covering 85% of our top 100 U.S. markets. ARPU grew 2.1% to $58.50, propelled by premium unlimited plans bundled with 5G Mobile Edge Computing services and fixed wireless access trials, which added 450,000 access lines. Compared to peers like Verizon and T-Mobile, our churn held steady at 0.79%, below the industry average of 0.95%, thanks to loyalty incentives tied to our AmpliFi Stream+ streaming integration. Regionally, U.S. wireless drove 92% of this segment, with early international traction in our Mexico JV contributing 8%, where we've deployed C-band spectrum to compete with América Móvil.

Broadband and wireline made up 28% of total revenues at $8.0 billion, up 7.2% year-over-year. This segment benefited from our aggressive fiber overbuild initiative, adding 1.8 million fiber passings to reach 45 million homes passed—on track for our 50 million target by 2025. Residential broadband revenues hit $5.3 billion, or 66% of the segment, with average revenue per account up 3.4% to $142, driven by gigabit-speed tiers and multi-gig upgrades amid surging demand for remote work and cloud gaming. Business wireline grew 12% to $2.7 billion, capturing enterprise share through SD-WAN and private 5G campus networks for Fortune 500 clients adopting Industry 4.0. In North America, this segment accounted for 95% of contribution; Europe operations, post our Vodafone UK acquisition integration, added modest 5% exposure but face regulatory headwinds from Ofcom's pricing reviews.

Media and entertainment represented 18% of total revenues at $5.2 billion, up 2.9% year-over-year. While moderating from pandemic peaks, this segment stabilized with 3.2 million domestic streaming subscriber adds for our AmpliFi Stream+ platform, now at 65 million paid subs globally—closing the gap with Netflix but outpacing Disney+ in ad-supported tiers. Linear TV revenues of $2.8 billion declined 4% due to cord-cutting, down 1.1 million video subs, offset by retransmission consent hikes and our expanded sports rights portfolio, including NBA and NFL synergies akin to our legacy satellite assets. Advertising revenues surged 15% to $1.2 billion, boosted by connected TV inventory and data-driven targeting via our Snowflake-powered ad platform. Regionally, U.S. dominates at 78%, with APAC growth via partnerships like JioCinema in India contributing 12%, where short-form video and regional content localization counter TikTok dominance.

Enterprise solutions contributed 9% at $2.6 billion, up 9.5% year-over-year, a high-growth area with double-digit expansion from cloud interconnects, IoT managed services, and cybersecurity bundles sold to hyperscalers and SLED sectors. Key wins include a $500 million multi-year deal for 5G private networks with logistics giants mirroring FedEx's deployments. Margins here expanded 250 basis points to 42% EBITDA, reflecting our shift from commoditized connectivity to value-added services like AI-optimized network slicing.

Other categories, including eliminations and corporate, accounted for 3% at $0.9 billion, flat year-over-year, primarily from equipment sales, wholesale peering, and spectrum lease-ups.

Year-over-year, the mix shifted two points from media toward wireless and broadband, improving blended EBITDA margins by 110 basis points to 40.1%. This diversification mitigates risks from linear TV erosion—now just 10% of total revenues versus 15% in 2022—while capitalizing on secular tailwinds like 5G SA core deployments live in 20 metros, Open RAN trials with Nokia and Ericsson cutting opex 20%, and fiber M&A like our $8 billion rural buildout via BEAD funding. Internationally, we're prioritizing high-ARPU markets; Latin America and Europe now 15% of revenues, up from 12%, but U.S. core remains 82% with superior 45% EBITDA margins. Looking forward, we expect Q1 wireless ARPU uplift from device refresh cycles like iPhone bundles and broadband acceleration via RDOF subsidies. Risks include spectrum auction dynamics—we've bid aggressively in the ongoing C-band roundup—and competitive pricing from cable peers like Charter. Our capex guidance holds at 15-16% of revenues for FY2024, focused on densifying 6GHz mmWave for fixed wireless broadband to challenge Starlink in underserved areas. This revenue mix positions AmpliFi for sustainable 4-6% organic growth through 2025, blending telecom scale with media relevance.

Shifting to ARPU trends, which have been pivotal in driving sustainable revenue growth across our 120 million subscriber base. Our blended postpaid ARPU—including mobile, fixed broadband, and video services—rose 4.2% year-over-year to $64.30 in Q4. This marks the fifth consecutive quarter of expansion, outpacing the industry average of 2-3% as reported by peers like Verizon and Comcast.

By segment, mobile postpaid ARPU increased 3.8% year-over-year to $56.80, driven by targeted pricing on our Unlimited Plus and Ultra plans, which now include 5G Advanced and mmWave access. We've seen strong uptake, with 65% of postpaid mobile subs on premium tiers, up from 52% a year ago. Fixed broadband ARPU rose 5.1% to $82.50, fueled by our FTTH rollout covering 45% of our footprint and pricing discipline amid bandwidth demand from remote work and streaming—gigabit speeds now the norm for 70% of our base, commanding a $15-20 premium over DSL. Video and media ARPU for standalone AmpliFi Stream+ grew 6.7% to $18.40, reflecting ad-tier pricing at $7.99/month and our new sports add-on at $9.99, with 2.5 million subs mirroring Peacock's success.

These gains stem directly from our pricing and bundling playbook, refined through data analytics and A/B testing. On pricing, inflationary pressures and supply chain normalization restored power after competitive discounting. In Q4, we implemented selective mid-cycle increases of 5-7% on 40% of mobile plans—similar to T-Mobile's moves—and 4-6% on broadband tiers. Phased regionally, U.S. pricing saw no meaningful churn elasticity, with disconnects at 0.8% post-hike versus 1.2% industry average. In Europe via our Vodafone JV markets like UK, Germany, and Italy, we delivered a 4.5% year-over-year ARPU lift to €28.50 ($31.00 equivalent), aided by EU spectrum auctions. In price-sensitive APAC like India and Indonesia JVs, we held to 3% increases, focusing on volume.

Bundling is where we're pulling ahead—quad-play bundles (mobile + fiber + video + IoT/security) now 55% of revenue, up from 42% year-over-year, boosting blended ARPU by an incremental $8.20 per sub. Our AmpliFi One Bundle at $120/month for Unlimited mobile, 1Gig fiber, AmpliFi Stream+ Premium with HBO Max and Paramount+ licensing, and Nest security hit 18 million U.S. households, driving $4.50 incremental ARPU from cross-sell, akin to Charter's Spectrum One but with deeper media ties. The new 5G Media StreamMax tier bundles ad-supported streaming with 100GB hotspot, lifting mobile ARPU by $3.10 for 12 million adopters, leveraging edge CDN with Akamai for 4K/HDR latency reduction. For B2B, SD-WAN + private 5G slices with Microsoft Teams added $25 ARPU uplift, now 15% of total.

Regionally, U.S. ARPU grew 4.8% to $68.20, outpacing Europe’s 3.2% to $32.80 amid regulatory caps, while Latin America lagged at 2.1% to $22.50 due to forex but improved via bundles with local video. Strategically, we're doubling down on AI-driven dynamic pricing via our RevOptix platform, personalizing offers for 7-10% lift. Open RAN and 5G SA covering 60% of U.S. sites by year-end enable low-latency bundles like AR/VR media. Churn at 1.1% validates this; for Q1 2024, we guide 3.5-4.5% blended growth, with bundles at 60% mix, supporting mid-teens EBITDA margins as capex moderates.

Next, as we pivot to forward-looking guidance, our EBITDA margin outlook remains a cornerstone of our profitability story. For context, Q4 adjusted EBITDA margin was 40.1%, up 120 basis points sequentially and 250 basis points year-over-year, driven by cost controls, premiumization of 5G and fiber, and synergies from our StreamForge Media acquisition bolstering converged offerings.

Looking ahead to Q1 2024, we guide adjusted EBITDA margin of 39.5% to 40.5%, a sequential expansion of 40 to 140 basis points. On a full-year FY2024 basis, we expect 39.0% to 39.5%, a 200 basis point improvement over FY2023's 37.1%. This embeds conviction in operational leverage as we lap peak capex from nationwide 5G SA and C-band deployment.

Key tailwinds: Revenue mix shift and ARPU expansion, with postpaid mobile up 4.2% to $58.50 on 65% 5G Ultra Wideband uptake and FWA bundles adding 28% broadband net adds. StreamForge's ad-supported tier ramps to 15 million subs by quarter-end, with uplift from zero-rating Disney+ and Netflix via 5G edge caching—yielding 300 basis points margin from recurring services. Opex efficiency from 'Network 2.0' realized $450 million run-rate savings year-to-date, with AI orchestration via Nokia/Ericsson Open RAN cutting site maintenance 18% and energy 22%. Bad debt down 15% via eKYC and ML fraud detection, scaled to enterprise 5G private networks.

Capex discipline holds FY2024 at $14.5-15 billion, or 15-16% of revenue, down from 18% as 95% 5G coverage hits. Prioritizing return-on-fiber with 45% broadband penetration in 20-state FTTx, targeting 50% by Q1 end; edge pilots with AWS Outposts add $150 million high-margin enterprise revenue.

Headwinds managed: Content costs sticky at 8% year-over-year, but multi-year NBA/Premier League deals cap at CPI+2%, offset 40% by FAST channels with 25% eCPM rise from CTV standards. North America (75% revenue) drives 80% expansion with 5G pricing; Europe (15%) capped at 35% by Gigabit Act unbundling, but Vodafone Germany JV deleverages via towers; APAC/LatAm (10%) at 32% from forex/competition, but Brazil 5G FWA projects 500 basis points FY2025 expansion via subsidies.

This trajectory funds 12-15% FCF yield in FY2025, $8 billion buybacks, and 4.5% dividend hike, emulating Comcast post-NBCU while outpacing Charter (37.8%) and T-Mobile (34.5%). Risks like spectrum renewals and tariffs mitigated by domestic supply chains.

Now, free cash flow generation and utilization, a cornerstone of our financial strength. For full year 2023, we generated $14.2 billion in free cash flow, up 18% from $12.0 billion in 2022, equating to 8.2% FCF yield on average market cap—above peer 6.5% per S&P Global.

Generation drivers: Adjusted operating cash flow hit $28.7 billion, up 12% year-over-year, from 4% wireless net adds—postpaid mobility and FWA—and 2.8% blended ARPU to $58.40 on 5G Ultra Wideband and AmpliFi Stream+ bundling. DTC streaming with 45 million global subs added $2.1 billion incremental cash from hits like EchoVerse and Disney+ Hotstar-like India JV.

Capex efficiency key: $14.5 billion deployed, 16.8% of revenue, down from 18.2%. High-ROI focus: $6.2 billion on 5G C-band in top 100 U.S. markets, $4.1 billion FTTH passing 15 million new locations (up 25%), $2.8 billion edge computing for low-latency media/cloud gaming. Open RAN in 40% new sites cut vendor costs 15% vs. Huawei/Ericsson; AI network slicing boosted spectral efficiency 22%, lifting margins to 42.1%.

Regionally, North America drove 72% or $10.2 billion, via StreamNet acquisition synergies like Comcast Peacock. EMEA $2.4 billion, up 22% on 5G SA in UK/Germany, 28% enterprise private networks share per EU Digital Decade. APAC $1.6 billion, 35% surge from 5G FWA adding 8 million Indonesia/India households, outpacing Reliance Jio rural.

Utilization balanced: 42% or $6.0 billion to dividends, with 10% quarterly hike to $0.65/share yielding 4.8% like AT&T post-spin. Share repurchases 28% or $4.0 billion, retiring 3.2% shares under $10 billion authorization, aiding 15% TSR outperformance vs. S&P Telecom Index. Debt reduction 18% or $2.6 billion, net debt/EBITDA to 2.4x from 2.7x for FCC C-band Phase II/Europe 3.5 GHz auctions. Remaining 12% or $1.6 billion for M&A: $900 million Latin content rights vs. Netflix, $700 million 6G NTN R&D with Starlink-like LEO partners.

Forward, FY2024 FCF $15.8-16.5 billion, 11-16% growth as capex to 15-16%, supporting $7 billion shareholder returns including specials, AI personalization boosting CPMs 20%, quantum-secure backhaul. 98% FCF conversion de-risks cord-cutting, positioning us in streaming-telecom wars.

Operator, we'd now be happy to take questions on this or any other topic.

Operator: Thank you. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. Our first question comes from David Lee with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

David Lee: Good morning. Can you provide more color on the ARPU trends and how bundling is impacting churn going forward?

Johnathan Reed: Certainly, David. Our bundling strategies, like the AmpliFi One quad-play and StreamMax 5G media tiers, have not only driven the 4.2% blended ARPU growth to $64.30 but also kept churn at a low 1.1%, well below peers. With penetration rising to 55% of revenue, we're seeing incremental $8.20 per sub uplift, and our AI dynamic pricing tests point to further gains without elasticity issues.

Operator: Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Emily Chen: Hi, thanks for taking my question. Could you elaborate on your plans for EBITDA margin guidance and free cash flow utilization in FY2024?

Michael Torres: Yes, Emily. We're guiding Q1 EBITDA margins to 39.5-40.5% and FY2024 to 39-39.5%, fueled by opex savings, ARPU expansion, and capex moderation to 15-16% of revenue. On FCF, expect $15.8-16.5 billion, with balanced use: heavy on dividends and buybacks totaling $7 billion in shareholder returns, plus debt paydown and tuck-in M&A for content and 6G, maintaining our 2.4x leverage for auctions.

Sarah Johnson: Thank you for your questions. That concludes our Q&A session. Johnathan, would you like to provide closing remarks?

Johnathan Reed: Thank you. In closing, I am proud of our team's performance this quarter and full year. We are well-positioned to continue delivering value to our customers and shareholders through our converged 5G-media leadership, margin expansion, and strong FCF generation. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
